POSITION / ACTION

All stops are candidates, not surveyed locations. Stop clear of runners; never run backward, block the course or operate the camera downhill.

Heart rates are adjustable planning suggestions, not measured training zones or medical safety thresholds. Prioritize breathing, effort and symptoms. Stop and seek help for chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.

04Run light. Leave the pack at the hotel.

0 / 10 ready

Camera discipline: GO Ultra is optional, with a tested secure cap mount only. No handheld stick. Leave the Action Pod at the hotel for before/after the race. Film 15–30 seconds at a time; do not operate the camera downhill.

Water & snacks: Carry a small handheld bottle or soft flask. Confirm cup policy, refill stations and mandatory kit in the current race instructions. A small familiar snack is optional; no need to try a new gel. Drink to thirst and conditions, not by force.

Clothing & layers: Tested shoes and socks, waist-pocket shorts and a light T-shirt. A light layer is useful for the ferry and waiting. Carry it on course if the actual wind, rain, temperature or mandatory-kit rules require it; the earlier weather estimate was not verified.

Medication & hotel bag: Carry only medication you personally need, including prescribed rescue medication if applicable—not a generic race medicine kit. Leave the 16L Osprey, dry clothes, toiletries, chargers and Action Pod at the hotel; confirm storage.

Taper & recovery reminders

Tuesday or Wednesday: 10-minute warm-up, 4–5 relaxed uphill efforts of 30–45 seconds with walk/jog recovery, then 5–10 minutes easy. Not a sprint workout. Rest Thursday and Friday; skip hills if still sore. Keep post-race meals and Sunday’s easy seaside walk flexible.

Insurance check: verify US coverage, organized amateur road/trail racing, emergency care and ambulance services in the policy wording. A product name is not proof of coverage. Recheck weather and ferry schedules before departure.

05Ask the coach

Data, route differences & limitations

Archived attachment, not the confirmed current course: The attachment was a MapMyRun webpage despite its GPX name. Only route coordinates and distances were recovered; duplicate navigation points and Water markers were removed. No attachment scripts were run or authentication fields retained. Route: Catalina Island Half - 10K, ID 2887761421, embedded update 2020-12-10. The public page lists 6.12 mi and 763 ft ascent[[6.1 mi Running Route in Avalon, California - MapMyRun]]。

Distance & ascent: Kilometer markers use the attachment’s cumulative distances. Noisy point elevations should not simply be added into an ascent total. The DEM profile is for terrain planning, not official course surveying.

Real contours: Contours come from public Terrarium DEM tiles, not interpolation of the route line: 10 m intervals at zoom 14. USGS terrain and global NOAA data are supplied through the Mapzen pipeline. Resolution, smoothing and platform algorithms explain differences[[Joerd terrain attribution]]。

Planning, not a promise: Pace, heart rate and photo stops are suggestions. Without measured maximum HR, threshold or race-day conditions, 160 bpm cannot be treated as a medical safety limit. The original 0–3 / 3–6.5 / 6.5–finish divisions do not match the attachment’s terrain, so the stages were revised.

Photography & privacy: Compositions are original SVG sketches, not site photographs. Bay visibility and stopping points are unverified. GPS and artwork are embedded; no map API, location or external-model requests are made. Checklist and language preferences stay in this browser. The page still contains personal plans; review visibility before public publishing.

Check against: Race courses · Original Strava route · Visual reference. This page is an independent implementation, not a copy of the reference source.
